title: Acute Panic Presentation Variant 27

patient.name: Mark Smith
patient.initial_statement: My heart is racing so fast and my chest feels extremely tight. I can't catch my breath, and I feel like I'm going to collapse.

symptoms: Severe chest tightness, rapid heart palpitations
Shortness of breath, feeling like suffocating (hyperventilating)
Numbness/tingling in fingers (paresthesias) and around mouth
Extreme sense of doom, dizziness, feeling of falling
medications: Alprazolam 0.25mg as needed for panic attacks
allergies: No known drug or food allergies
family_history: Mother has history of anxiety and panic disorder
social_history: Works long hours, high caffeine/energy drink intake
review_of_systems: Cardiovascular: pulse rate is 116 bpm, no active chest pain except as noted.

patient_beliefs: I hope this is just a temporary strain that will pass.
I've been under a lot of stress with my job.
I'm terrified this might be something permanent or fatal.
patient_goals: Determine the core cause of these symptoms.
Verify whether there is emergency intervention required.
Get diagnostic results explained to me step by step.

examinations.name: Neurological Examination
examinations.result: Grossly intact, though patient complains of finger numbness.

investigations.name: 12-Lead Electrocardiogram (ECG)
investigations.result: Sinus tachycardia with rate of 116 bpm bpm, normal axis, no ST change.

investigations.name: Complete Blood Count (CBC)
investigations.result: WBC: 6.4 x10^9/L, Hb: 13.8 g/dL, Platelets: 220 x10^9/L.
investigations.interpretation: Complete blood count is within normal references.

investigations.name: Serum Electrolytes Panel
investigations.interpretation: Serum electrolytes are within normal range.

investigations.name: Chest X-ray (CXR)
investigations.result: Both lungs are hypolucent, no vascular congestion or consolidation.

investigations.name: CT Angiography of Chest
investigations.result: Normal caliber aorta, no luminal narrowing, no dissection flap visible.

investigations.name: CT Scan of Head (cranial assessment)
investigations.result: No acute hemorrhage, infarct, or midline shifts found in cranial structures.
investigations.interpretation: Normal CT Scan of the Head.

investigations.name: CT Scan of Abdomen & Pelvis
investigations.result: Stomach, liver, bowel loops, and appendix are normal size with no inflammatory changes.
investigations.interpretation: Normal CT Scan of the Abdomen.

investigations.name: Urinalysis and Urine Culture
investigations.result: Clear yellow appearance, negative nitrite, negative leukocyte esterase.
investigations.interpretation: Urinalysis is clear of infection signs.

investigations.name: Duplex Vascular Leg Ultrasound
investigations.result: Normal patency of left and right femoral veins with complete color Doppler signal.

red_flags: Presence of alarm symptoms (e.g. weight loss, focal neuro signs)
